title: The Fundamental Unit of Life
seo_title: The Fundamental Unit of Life Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 9, Chapter 5: The Fundamental Unit of Life
standard_text: Cell – basic unit of life: prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, multicellular organisms; cell membrane and cell wall, cell organelles and cell inclusions; chloroplast, mitochondria, vacuoles, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus; nucleus, chromosomes – basic structure, number.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 5: cell theory, the plasma membrane, osmosis and diffusion, the cell wall, the nucleus, organelles such as mitochondria and plastids, and prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The cell is the basic unit of life.
key_sub: Mitochondria release energy; chloroplasts make food.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells, and every cell comes from an existing cell. A cell has a plasma membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus with chromosomes. Plant cells also have a cellulose cell wall, plastids such as chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

Water moves across the selectively permeable membrane by osmosis: a cell swells in a dilute (hypotonic) solution and shrinks in a concentrated (hypertonic) one. Organelles share the work: mitochondria release energy, ribosomes make proteins, the Golgi apparatus packages them and lysosomes digest waste. Prokaryotes such as bacteria have no nuclear membrane.

Example

A plant cell in strong salt solution?

water leaves by osmosis

Answer: plasmolysis: the cytoplasm shrinks from the wall

Example

Which organelle makes proteins?

the site of protein synthesis

Answer: ribosomes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking osmosis moves solute particles rather than water.
  • Saying animal cells have a cell wall.
  • Calling bacteria eukaryotes.

faq.q: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
faq.a: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have no nuclear membrane and no membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus and organelles.

faq.q: Why are lysosomes called suicide bags?
faq.a: If the cell is damaged, they can burst and their enzymes digest the cell itself.
